name: Prefix Sum
description: Precompute cumulative sums (or counts) over an array so that the sum of any subarray can be answered in O(1) instead of re-summing the range each time. Extends to hashmap-based prefix sums for 'subarray sums to k'-style problems.
core_technique: Build a prefix array where prefix[i] = sum of all elements up to index i. The sum of any range [l, r] is then prefix[r] - prefix[l-1] in O(1). For 'count subarrays summing to k' variants, use a hashmap tracking how many times each prefix sum value has occurred, since subarray(i+1, j) sums to k exactly when prefix[j] - prefix[i] = k.
common_pitfalls: Off-by-one errors on whether prefix[i] includes index i or not - pick a consistent convention (usually prefix[0] = 0, prefix[i] = sum of first i elements) and stick to it; forgetting to initialize the hashmap with {0: 1} for the subarray-sum-equals-k variant, which misses subarrays that start at index 0; recomputing the prefix array unnecessarily inside a loop instead of once upfront.

example_problems.title: Range Sum Query - Immutable
example_problems.why_it_fits: Textbook use case -- precompute prefix sums once, answer every range-sum query in O(1) instead of O(n) per query.

example_problems.title: Subarray Sum Equals K
example_problems.why_it_fits: Track running prefix sum and a hashmap of {prefix_sum: count_seen}; at each index, check whether (current_prefix - k) has been seen before -- if so, that many subarrays ending here sum to k.

example_problems.title: Corporate Flight Bookings
example_problems.why_it_fits: Uses the difference-array variant: instead of applying each booking's effect across its whole range, mark only the start (+seats) and end+1 (-seats), then take a prefix sum at the end to get the final per-day totals.

additional_considerations: Distinguish plain prefix sums (range sum queries on a static array) from the hashmap variant (counting subarrays matching a condition) -- they look similar but solve different question shapes. For range-update problems (add a value to every element in a range), the difference-array trick (mark boundaries, prefix-sum at the end) turns O(n) per update into O(1) per update.
